desc: Design a data structure that can update a Young diagram (down-right quadrant) in O(log^2 N) time, possibly using a 2D segment tree with lazy propagation storing the transformation for each node.
Alternatively, use a divide-and-conquer on the grid with a segment tree on rows/columns, or use a different recurrence representation to achieve O(log^2 N) per query.
Implement the optimized solution in Python with careful attention to constants (e.g., using iterative segment tree, avoiding recursion).
Test the solution on the provided sample inputs to ensure correctness.
If performance is still an issue, consider using PyPy-specific optimizations or rewriting the critical inner loops in a more efficient manner.
Implement the segment tree on the anti-diagonal flattened array with range update capability.

For each query, decompose the affected down-right quadrant into O(H+W) contiguous intervals on the anti-diagonals, compute the first cell's dp value directly, and update the rest using the segment tree.
Optimize the per-query update by reducing the number of anti-diagonals processed (e.g., using a segment tree over anti-diagonals to batch updates).
Consider using a 2D segment tree or a different flattening to achieve O(log^2 N) per query.
Profile and optimize the Python code for speed (e.g., using PyPy, reducing overhead in the inner loops).
